ab_kananaskis.blurb: Kananaskis lies east and south of Canmore, about an hour and a half by road from Calgary. Sport climbing dominates, mostly from 5.9 to 5.12 with the heaviest concentration at 5.10 and 5.11, plus a smaller number of trad lines, top-ropes and a winter ice and mixed scene. Wasootch Slabs is a relaxed, mostly top-rope and easy-grade area, with south-facing walls that dry quickly and catch the sun, a good late-winter or spring choice. Barrier Bluffs offers steeper sport lines, and the larger mountainsides such as Moose Mountain hold the most routes. Long alpine and semi-alpine multipitch lines are also part of the mix, and Evan Thomas Creek is the best-known ice area.

mt_kalispell_area.blurb: This part of northwest Montana takes in the Flathead Valley around Kalispell, Whitefish and Columbia Falls, plus the Libby and Eureka country, with the crags spread across roughly two hours of driving. Sport and trad lead the way, with a smaller group of boulders; most roped routes fall between 5.8 and 5.11, peaking around 5.10. Stone Hill is the largest area: very hard quartzite above Lake Koocanusa with edging faces, steep slabs and some cracks, nine main crags and plenty of top-rope-friendly lines. Point of Rocks is built on argillite, with hundreds of sport climbs plus trad and boulders linked by short hikes through rolling hills. Stryker and Stillwater Canyon is a cooler, shaded option for hot summer days.

co_glenwood_springs.blurb: Climbing around Glenwood Springs centres on Glenwood Canyon, where the Colorado River has cut through layers of limestone and Precambrian granite beside the interstate. Sport climbing is the largest share, with a solid amount of trad, some boulders and a little ice, and grades ranging widely from the 5.7 range up past 5.13, with most between 5.10 and 5.12. Limestone holds most of the sport climbing, including the Puoux, which climbs well year round, while the granite buttresses and cracks suit trad climbers who like a more adventurous outing. Waterfall ice forms when winter is cold enough. Main Elk Creek and East Elk Creek, away from the canyon, also hold a large share of the climbs.

co_ouray_vicinity_rock.blurb: Ouray sits at roughly 7,800 feet in the San Juan Mountains of Colorado, with climbing along the Uncompahgre River and its canyons. Ice is the largest single share and the Uncompahgre Gorge is the biggest sub-area, alongside a big sport-climbing scene and a notable amount of mixed and trad. Roped rock routes mostly run from 5.8 to 5.12, thickest at 5.10 and 5.11, with easier options for newer climbers. Crags face every direction, some are seasonal, and the popular ones can get busy. Pool Wall is the largest rock wall nearby, with Camp Bird Road, Rotary Park and Overlook Cliff also holding plenty of lines. Alpine objectives in the surrounding mountains add a bigger-day option.

ca_carson_pass_highway_88.blurb: This grouping runs along Highway 88 near Carson Pass, around 7,800 feet in the Sierra, with lakes, granite and wilderness terrain. Trad is the main style, followed by a strong bouldering showing and a smaller number of sport and top-rope routes; most roped climbs run from 5.8 to 5.11, thickest at 5.10, and boulders range from the easiest grades to the V10 range. Woodfords Canyon is the largest sub-area, known for steep granite and variety. Silver Lake is popular for top-roping, and Calaveras Domes offers tall multipitch lines. Some of the rock further out near the reservoir is obscure, with little published information, so expect a mix of roadside crags and more remote wilderness outings.

nl_avalon_peninsula.blurb: The Avalon Peninsula is the most populated and best-developed part of Newfoundland for climbing, centred on St. John's. Bouldering is the largest share, followed by sport and trad, with some ice and top-rope; roped routes mostly span 5.7 to 5.12 and peak around 5.10, while problems range from the easiest grades up to V10, with many moderates. Flatrock, a short drive north of St. John's, is the biggest sub-area: sea cliffs and boulders over the open Atlantic, on dense conglomerate sandstone rather than the limestone found elsewhere on the island. Gear can be tricky in that pebbly rock, and east-facing walls get morning sun. St. John's Area, Conception Bay South and Highway Barrens add more boulders.
